paragraphs: Five days after two catastrophic earthquakes struck Venezuela’s northern coast near Caracas, rescue teams are desperately searching the rubble for survivors.
While more than 1,700 people are confirmed dead, the final death toll is expected to rise significantly because approximately 46,000 people remain unaccounted for.

In coastal towns like Caraballeda, volunteers use specialized radar equipment and their bare hands to locate signs of life beneath collapsed buildings. Despite fading hopes, miraculous rescues keep families motivated. A mother and her baby were recently saved after being trapped for days; she kept her son alive by checking his breathing whenever he cried. However, at many disaster sites, official counting has paused.

Critics openly accuse the Venezuelan government of intentionally delaying the publication of accurate casualty numbers and point out a long history of systematically hiding bad news from the public. At the same time, thousands of families continue to wait in fear of bad news.

paragraphs: Two big earthquakes recently hit the coast of Venezuela near the capital city. Five days after the disaster, rescue workers and volunteers are still looking for people under collapsed buildings.

More than 1,700 people are dead, but the real number will be much higher because 46,000 people are still missing. In some towns, workers use special radar tools to hear people talking under the rocks. Families still have hope because of beautiful stories, like a mother and her small baby who were saved alive after days in the dark.
The searching is very difficult and slow. Many people say that the government is not telling the truth about the total number of dead people because they want to hide the bad news from the world.

paragraphs: Two big earthquakes hit Venezuela. The houses on the coast are broken. More than 1,700 people are dead, and 46,000 people are still missing.

Families are very sad, but they are still looking for their loved ones. Some workers use their hands and special machines to find people under the rocks. But there are happy stories, too. A mother and her baby come out alive after five days. The mother helps her baby stay strong.
People are angry at the leaders. They think that the leaders are lying about the bad news and the true number of dead people.
